import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HW = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HW, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * HW, HW, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HW, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        p = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

C3 = 16
WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.c1 = nn.Conv3d(8, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(C3, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.mix = nn.Conv2d(C3 * spec.Z, WIDTH, 1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        vox = torch.stack([obs[:, 0:Z], obs[:, Z:2 * Z], obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]], dim=1)
        bc = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zc = zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        v = torch.cat([vox, bc, zc], dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.c1(v))
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        f = F.relu(self.mix(h.reshape(B, C3 * Z, Y, X)))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

D = 48
HEADS = 4
MLP = 96


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_types = spec.n_types
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, D, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(D, D, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, spec.Y * spec.X, D))
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(D)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(D, 3 * D)
        self.out = nn.Linear(D, D)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(D)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(D, MLP), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(MLP, D))
        self.lnf = nn.LayerNorm(D)
        self.place_head = nn.Linear(D, spec.n_types)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * D, D), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(D, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(D, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        B = f.shape[0]
        h = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos
        N = h.shape[1]
        dh = D // HEADS
        qkv = self.qkv(self.ln1(h)).view(B, N, 3, HEADS, dh).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q, k, v = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]
        att = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(dh), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(att, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, D)
        h = h + self.out(o)
        h = h + self.mlp(self.ln2(h))
        h = self.lnf(h)
        place = self.place_head(h).transpose(1, 2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean(1), h.amax(1)], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HW = 24
SK = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.skip = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, SK, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + SK, HW, (dy, dx)), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HW, 1, 1))
            for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

        u = torch.cat([f, self.skip(obs)], dim=1)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            q = F.pad(u, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            outs.append(head(q))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

W = 24
HW = 16
GW = 64
W2 = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(10, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.gproj = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(W, HW, (dy, dx)), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HW, 1, 1))
            for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        for hd in self.heads:
            nn.init.zeros_(hd[2].weight)
            nn.init.zeros_(hd[2].bias)
        self.body2 = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W2, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.head2 = nn.Conv2d(W2, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * W2, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        T = len(self.fps)
        b = obs[:, 0:Z]
        t = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        m = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        e = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        below = F.pad(b, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        tab = F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))[:, 1:]
        per = torch.stack([b, t, m, e, below, tab], dim=2)
        bc = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, 3, Y, X)
        zc = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zc = zc.view(1, Z, 1, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, 1, Y, X)
        v = torch.cat([per, bc, zc], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 10, Y, X)
        g0 = self.gproj(obs).unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, W, Y, X).reshape(B * Z, W, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.c1(v) + g0)
        h = h + F.relu(self.c2(h))
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            q = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            outs.append(head(q))
        s = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).reshape(B, Z, T, Y, X)
        f2 = self.body2(obs)
        place = (torch.logsumexp(s, dim=1) + self.head2(f2)).flatten(1)
        hv = h.reshape(B, Z, W, Y, X)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([hv.mean((1, 3, 4)), hv.amax((1, 3, 4)),
                                 f2.mean((2, 3)), f2.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HW = 24


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HW, (dy, dx)) for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HW, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, HW * len(self.fps))
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        pooled = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        c = self.ctx(pooled)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            q = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            ci = c[:, i * HW:(i + 1) * HW, None, None]
            hh = F.relu(self.convs[i](q) + ci)
            outs.append(self.outs[i](hh))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(pooled)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + SK, HW, (dy, dx)), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HW, 1, 1))
            for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.skip = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, SK, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.gate = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        h = h + F.relu(self.c2(h))
        c = self.ctx(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        h = h + F.relu(self.c3(h + c[:, :, None, None]))
        s = self.skip(obs) * self.gate
        u = torch.cat([h, s], dim=1)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            q = F.pad(u, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            outs.append(head(q))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: compact kernel-head actor + separate critic
trials.hypothesis: New idea: separate the actor's and critic's features. The actor uses a cheaper width-48 two-conv body with the footprint-kernel head and a DONE head. The critic has its own small width-32 conv trunk. Gradients from value regression then cannot distort the placement features, and the cheaper actor keeps the cost near 1.1x, so it trains for more steps. Refuted if its 4-seed mean is no better than r2c2.
trials.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HW = 24
CW = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HW, (dy, dx)), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HW, 1, 1))
            for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.critic_body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, CW, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(CW, CW, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.critic_glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * CW, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            q = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            outs.append(head(q))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        cf = self.critic_body(obs)
        cg = self.critic_glob(torch.cat([cf.mean((2, 3)), cf.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        return logits, self.value_head(cg).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, and scores are hidden, so these first trials are chosen by reasoning alone. Most networks costing about 1.0–1.4x the baseline still get roughly the full step budget. In this task a placement is right when the brick lands, at the highest build height under its footprint, on a layer where the target fills every footprint cell. The baseline's 1x1 head sees only the anchor cell's features. It never pools over the brick's footprint, and its weights for each layer are separate rather than shared. I'm testing three cheap fixes: (1) a head that pools features over each brick's footprint, (2) a deeper residual body at the same cost with the global summary fed back into the cells, and (3) a 3D convolution body that shares its weights across layers. All three stay close to the baseline's compute so they lose few training steps.
analyses.2: Scores are hidden, and all three round-1 trials trained without errors, so success does not tell them apart. All three were cheap (1.05–1.22x), so they kept most of the training steps. Without scores, I'll choose by prior reasoning and spread the risk across distinct ideas while keeping compute near 1.1–1.3x. Placement mostly depends on two things. The first is local: whether the cells under a footprint land on the right layer and match the target there. The second is global: the build order (lower layers and supports first) and when to choose DONE. This round has three candidates: (1) combine the two round-1 ideas that address these needs separately, the footprint-pooled head and the residual body with global broadcast; (2) a footprint-shaped conv head that keeps track of which footprint cell holds which feature (pooling loses this), useful for overhangs and partial matches; (3) a new idea, one self-attention block over cells for long-range context, which none of the round-1 trials covered.
analyses.3: No scores are visible, and all six trials trained without errors. So the ranking has to rest on priors about the task. Two things decide whether a placement is right. One is where the brick lands, which is the maximum height under its footprint. The other is whether every footprint cell at that layer matches the target. The footprint-aware heads (r1c1 pooling, r2c2 footprint-sized kernels) encode this directly, and r2c2's kernel version also keeps track of which cell is which. The residual body with a global vector (r1c2) adds context for build order and DONE. Untested so far: the kernel head on the residual-global body, giving the head exact raw height and target information, and scoring each layer separately with weights shared across layers so the network can learn "lands at z and matches the target at z". All three proposals stay at or below about 1.4x compute so the step count stays close to the full budget.
analyses.4: No success scores are visible, so I can't rank the trials. All 9 trained without errors and stayed between 1.05x and 1.38x the starting compute. Each idea has been tested only in one or two variants. The task argues for one design choice: an exact build needs the head to check landing height and target match on every cell a brick covers. The footprint-kernel head, which keeps track of which cell holds which feature, is the best fit for that. A global view helps decide build order and when to choose DONE. With 3 trials left, all three use the footprint-kernel head: (A) r2c2 plus a global context vector added into the head; (B) the strongest combination so far, residual-global body plus kernel head plus raw-obs skip; (C) a new idea, a cheaper shared trunk with a separate critic trunk so value learning does not disturb the policy features. I kept all three near 1.1–1.35x so they get close to the full step budget.
